title: What does ASIC RG 105 require of an AFS licensee's responsible managers?
description: How ASIC assesses AFS organizational competence under RG 105: responsible managers, the five knowledge and skills options, records, and the 2026 FAR change.
shortAnswer: Regulatory Guide 105 (RG 105) explains how the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) assesses the organizational competence obligation in section 912A(1)(e) of the Corporations Act 2001. An Australian financial services (AFS) licensee must nominate responsible managers who make significant day to day decisions, who together cover every authorized service and product, and who each meet one of five knowledge and skills options combining qualifications with years of relevant experience.
keyTakeaways: Organizational competence (s912A(1)(e)) is a licensee level obligation, separate from the s912A(1)(f) duty to train representatives, which RG 104 and RG 146 cover.

Each responsible manager must meet both the knowledge and the skills component of one of five options. Options 1, 3 and 4 need three years of relevant experience in the past five; Option 2 needs five years in the past eight.
ASIC expects at least two responsible managers in most businesses, allows up to 20, and imposes a key person condition where a licensee depends heavily on one or two people.
Licensees must review competence regularly and on any change, keep responsible managers' knowledge current, and keep records of both, under condition 4 of the standard license conditions.
From October 16, 2026 ASIC reduced the competence evidence that FAR accountable persons must submit as responsible managers. An updated RG 105 is expected in Quarter 1 of 2027.
appliesTo: Australian financial services licensees and AFS license applicants
Responsible managers nominated on an AFS license, including key persons
Responsible entities and operators of registered schemes, IDPSs and corporate collective investment vehicles (CCIVs)
Banks, insurers and other APRA regulated licensees whose accountable persons also act as responsible managers

sections.heading: What is the organizational competence obligation?

blocks.text: The organizational competence obligation requires an AFS licensee to maintain the competence to provide every financial service its license covers, and ASIC tests it by looking at the knowledge and skills of the licensee's responsible managers. [RG 105 AFS licensing: Organisational competence](https://asic.gov.au/regulatory-resources/find-a-document/regulatory-guides/rg-105-licensing-organisational-competence/) was issued on June 23, 2022 and ties the obligation to section 912A(1)(e) of the [Corporations Act 2001](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A00818/latest/text) (RG 105.4 to RG 105.5).

RG 105 is explicit that it does not deal with the separate obligation in section 912A(1)(f) to ensure representatives are trained and competent (RG 105.3). That obligation is covered by RG 104 and, for retail advice, by RG 146 and the adviser professional standards, which are explained on the pages about [RG 146 training standards](/regulations/asic-rg-146-training-requirements) and [financial adviser education and CPD](/regulations/financial-adviser-education-and-cpd-requirements). In short: RG 146 asks whether the people serving clients are trained; RG 105 asks whether the people running the business are competent to run it.

The obligation bites at two points. An applicant must show it can comply from the day the license is granted, and ASIC cannot grant a license if it has reason to believe the applicant is likely not to comply (s913B(1)(b), RG 105.12). After licensing, competence must be maintained at all times, and ASIC may suspend or cancel the license or impose conditions under sections 915C(1)(a) and 914A(1) if it is not (RG 105.13). A breach or likely breach may also be a reportable situation under section 912DAA (RG 105.15).

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects RG 105 as issued on June 23, 2022 and the notice ASIC added to the guide's web page, as at November 2026. ASIC states the guide is being updated for Financial Accountability Regime changes and expects the new version in Quarter 1 of 2027. Check the primary sources before relying on any paragraph number.

sections.heading: Who can be nominated as a responsible manager?

blocks.text: A responsible manager must be directly responsible for significant day to day decisions about the ongoing provision of the licensee's financial services, must meet one of the five knowledge and skills options, and must be fit and proper (RG 105.8 and the key points to Section B). Titles do not matter; the level of direct responsibility does.

items: **Time and involvement:** ASIC looks at whether a nominee already acts as a responsible manager or key person elsewhere and whether they have enough time for the role. The more commitments a person has, the less likely ASIC is to accept them (RG 105.26 to RG 105.27).

**Number:** ASIC expects at least two responsible managers, although it may accept one for a one person advisory business or where financial services are not the main business. No more than 20 can be nominated at any time (RG 105.49 to RG 105.51).

**Combined coverage:** collectively, the responsible managers must have knowledge and skills for every financial service and product authorized. One person can cover life insurance and another general insurance, but each must still meet an option (RG 105.39 to RG 105.43).

**Small, heavily automated businesses:** a responsible manager who reviews and signs off rather than making daily decisions may be accepted in limited circumstances, but must be named as a key person (RG 105.28 to RG 105.35).
**Scheme and CCIV operators:** responsible managers must collectively cover both the compliance obligations of the service and the kinds of assets under management (RG 105.44 and RG 105.55).

sections.heading: What are the five options for demonstrating knowledge and skills?

blocks.text: Each option pairs a knowledge component, usually a qualification or course, with a skills component, usually a minimum period of relevant experience, and a responsible manager must meet both halves of the same option (RG 105.54). The table reproduces ASIC's Table 1 with the paragraph references that explain each option.

blocks.text: Experience counts only if it is practical experience in deciding how the relevant services or products are provided and either providing them or supervising those who do (RG 105.57). The ASIC Training Register, which RG 105 still refers to for short courses and assessors, is valid only up to September 24, 2012, so licensees must check post 2012 courses directly with providers and show their relevance to the manager's role (RG 105.84 to RG 105.86). Overseas qualifications are accepted if comparable to an Australian qualification that meets an option (RG 105.59).

sections.heading: What must a licensee do to keep its responsible managers competent?

blocks.text: A licensee must have documented measures that review organizational competence regularly and whenever responsible managers or business activities change, maintain and update responsible managers' knowledge and skills, and keep records of both the reviews and the steps taken (RG 105.10). This expectation sits behind condition 4 of the standard license conditions in Pro Forma 209 (RG 105.9).

RG 105 sets no minimum CPD hours for AFS responsible managers, unlike RG 206 for credit licensees. The licensee decides how knowledge is kept current, and ASIC may check those measures during surveillance (RG 105.14). ASIC also says documentation matters: "it is more difficult to show compliance when documentation is not in place" (RG 105.11). A [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) that lists each responsible manager against the authorizations they cover is the simplest way to show that combined coverage has no gaps.

Review is also expected before the business changes, for example before adding a product authorization or replacing a responsible manager (RG 105.16). Every addition or removal of a responsible manager must be notified to ASIC using Form FS20, and where the person is named as a key person the licensee must also apply to vary the key person condition using Form FS03 (RG 105.115 to RG 105.116). If a key person leaves, condition 3 of Pro Forma 209 requires the licensee to nominate a replacement or explain why not, and to show it still has competence for all its services (RG 105.114).

sections.heading: What evidence should a licensee keep for each RG 105 obligation?

blocks.text: Evidence should show, for every responsible manager, which option they meet, which authorizations they cover, and how their knowledge has been kept current since nomination. blocks.text: Keeping these records in a structured register makes them usable for breach assessments as well as for ASIC surveillance. The guide to [preparing training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) explains how to version evidence so that a reviewer can see what was true on a given date.

sections.heading: How does the Financial Accountability Regime change RG 105?

blocks.text: From October 16, 2026, responsible managers who are also accountable persons under the Financial Accountability Regime Act 2023 (FAR Act) face reduced requirements to submit evidence of competence when an AFS license application is lodged through the ASIC Regulatory Portal. ASIC's notice on the RG 105 page says the change "streamline[s] responsible manager AFS licensing requirements for entities subject to the FAR Act" and that the updated guide is expected in Quarter 1 of 2027.

Two points follow. First, the change reduces what must be submitted, not the underlying section 912A(1)(e) obligation, so the licensee still needs internal evidence that each person meets an option and that coverage is complete. Second, until the revised guide is published, the June 2022 text remains the published statement of ASIC's expectations. Entities subject to FAR can align their accountability statements and their responsible manager coverage map so the same capability evidence supports both.

sections.heading: Does RG 105 apply to credit licensees?

blocks.text: No. Australian credit licensees have a parallel organizational competence obligation under section 47(1)(f) of the National Consumer Credit Protection Act 2009, explained in ASIC's [RG 206 Credit licensing: Competence and training](https://asic.gov.au/regulatory-resources/find-a-document/regulatory-guides/rg-206-credit-licensing-competence-and-training/). Its minimum is different: responsible managers need at least two years of relevant problem free experience and a credit industry qualification at Certificate IV level or a higher general qualification, plus at least 20 hours of CPD each year (RG 206.7 and RG 206.12).

A business holding both licenses therefore needs two sets of responsible manager evidence assessed against two different guides. The [mortgage broker best interests duty page](/regulations/mortgage-broker-best-interests-duty-training) covers the credit side in more detail.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models each license authorization, each responsible manager and the RG 105 option they rely on as linked records in one framework. When a manager leaves or an authorization is added, the uncovered products and the evidence needed to close the gap are identified from the framework rather than reconstructed from personnel files.

faqs.q: Is there a CPD hours requirement for AFS responsible managers?
faqs.a: RG 105 does not set a number of hours. It expects the licensee to maintain and update responsible managers' knowledge and skills and to keep records of the steps taken. Responsible managers who are also relevant providers giving personal advice to retail clients meet the separate adviser CPD standard in their adviser capacity.

faqs.q: Can a responsible manager rely on an old ASIC Training Register course?
faqs.a: Yes, if the course is still relevant to the role. RG 105 says the register is valid only up to September 24, 2012 and is no longer current, so for later courses the licensee must check with the provider and be able to show the course is relevant to the manager's role.

faqs.q: What happens if a key person leaves?
faqs.a: The standard key person condition requires the licensee to nominate a replacement responsible manager, or explain to ASIC why it has not, and to show it still has organizational competence for all its financial services and products. The licensee must also apply to vary the condition using Form FS03.

faqs.q: Do responsible managers have to be directors?
faqs.a: No. RG 105 says titles and job descriptions vary and that responsible managers need direct responsibility for significant day to day decisions about the financial services. Senior managers or heads of business units often fill the role, while directors without that direct involvement usually do not.

faqs.q: Does the FAR change remove the need to meet an option?
faqs.a: ASIC describes the October 16, 2026 change as reducing requirements to submit evidence of competence for responsible managers who are FAR accountable persons. It does not describe removing the organizational competence obligation itself, so licensees should keep internal evidence until the updated guide confirms the detail.
